richText.rubyHint: Select text in the box above, type its reading, then click Add reading. It is written as [漢字|かんじ].
richText.syntaxHint: Syntax: [漢字|かんじ] for furigana / pinyin, **bold**, _italic_; line breaks are kept.

typeHints.SingleChoice: Learners pick exactly one option. Mark the correct one.
typeHints.MultipleChoice: Learners pick every correct option; points only when the selection is exactly right.
typeHints.TrueFalse: One statement; learners answer True or False.
typeHints.FillBlank: Write [[1]], [[2]]… in the stem where learners type; each blank has its own accepted answers and scores on its own.
typeHints.Matching: Match each left item with a right item; points are shared by correct pairs.
typeHints.Ordering: Enter the items in the correct order; learners see them shuffled.
typeHints.ShortAnswer: Compared with the accepted answers; answers that do not match go to the teacher.
typeHints.Essay: Graded by the teacher (optionally with a rubric of the paper).

banks.title: Question banks
banks.subtitle: Questions per language, reused across papers.
banks.formHint: Name, language and who may see the bank.
banks.name: Bank name
banks.visibilityHint: Private: you and assessment managers. Shared: every author of the center can see and use it.
banks.emptyHint: Create your first bank, then add questions to it.

groups.title: Reading groups
groups.hint: One passage shared by several questions.

question.sheetHint: Each save creates a new version; attempts already given keep their version.
question.empty: This bank has no questions yet
question.blankHint: Mark blanks as [[1]], [[2]]… in order, without gaps.
question.rightHint: Extra items can be added as distractors.
question.blanks: {count, plural, =0 {No blanks yet} one {# blank} other {# blanks}}
question.noBlanks: Add [[1]] to the stem to create a blank.
question.blanksGap: Blank numbers must run from [[1]] without gaps (e.g. [[1]], [[2]], [[3]]).
question.acceptedHint: One accepted answer per line. List both kana and kanji spellings (or simplified / traditional) when both are right.
question.shortAnswerHint: One answer per line. Other answers go to the teacher.
question.tagsHint: Comma separated, e.g. n5, lesson 3, grammar.
question.explanationHint: Shown to learners when answers are visible (optional).

papers.title: Papers
papers.subtitle: Combine fixed questions, reading groups and random draws into a paper, then assign it to classes.
papers.summary: {sections, plural, one {# section} other {# sections}} · {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
papers.frameworkHint: Used to pick skills and levels for sections and random draws.
papers.showRuby: Show furigana / pinyin while taking the test
papers.showRubyHint: Turn off for JLPT-style papers, where reading kanji is part of the test.
papers.emptyHint: Build a paper from the questions of your banks.

sections.title: Sections
sections.timeHint: Time limits: set one on every section (each runs on its own clock) or leave all empty.

items.empty: This section has no questions yet.
items.question: Question
items.tagsHint: Comma separated; leave empty to draw from the whole bank.
items.randomHint: Each learner gets this many questions drawn from the bank (archived questions and reading-group questions are skipped).
items.randomTitle: {count, plural, one {# random question} other {# random questions}} from {bank}
items.pointsHint: Leave empty to use the question's points.
items.noBanks: No banks for this language yet.
items.unknownQuestion: Question no longer available (archived or not visible)

rubrics.title: Rubrics
rubrics.hint: Grade essays and short answers per criterion (e.g. IELTS: 4 criteria, band 9).
rubrics.name: Rubric name

errors.assessment_points_invalid: Points must be above 0 and at most 1000.
errors.assessment_essay_limits_invalid: Length limits are not valid (the minimum cannot exceed the maximum).
